config.title: Dominion bv-v1: Buy Value
config.goal_text: at least 53% against both RL-v3 c1 2300 and c2 2654 on 2,000 reserved kingdoms, both seats, 95% interval above 50%

chart.y_label: score % (student on c2 vs c2, 600 dev games)

charts.title: Dev regret (teacher points lost by the pick)

runs.note: Distil a paired-rollout buy teacher into a Deep Sets student on top of RL-v3 c2.

decisions.title: Review fixes implemented
decisions.text: Labels: deterministic seeds, replay key per row (kingdom, seed, seat, opponent, decision index), settings and model hashes in every shard, explicit candidate mask and live prior, per-candidate cap counts, rollouts with engine errors rejected, atomic shards, a crashed worker stops collection. Grader: adaptive draws use the exact paired SE between the actual top two. Validation: a frozen bank of dev positions regraded with 128 independent draws over all legal buys (experiments/bank.py); student and controls (experiments/controls.py: flat MLP, gain-only student, incumbent) are scored on it. Gates in code: pilot (caps/rejects < 1%, tests pass), DAgger only after an independent dev2 check, promotion on a fresh confirmation stream vs c2, c1 and the GA base (1-point tolerance) with latency p50/p95. Evaluation kingdoms are never collected and are dropped from training. Matches: resume only with an identical manifest; per-decision latency and per-override action log. Tests: observation equivalence (same observation, different hidden allocation -> identical grades; different observation -> different), replay reproduces the position. p1 goes back to stage 2 (DAgger was entered on one noisy dev point).
decisions.rejected: Known top cards after Harbinger/Sentry and a Steam-side availability contract: need reveal tracking in the engine; not done

decisions.title: Bug fix: the student's training prior did not match its live prior
decisions.text: Found by the implementation review: training rebuilt the candidate set with isnan(Q) in C, and -ffast-math let the compiler drop that check, so c2's prior spread over ungraded cards in training (76% of the mass off the candidates on 64 real rows) while play used the true candidates. Now an explicit candidate mask and the live prior are recorded with each label, teacher selection uses the mask, old shards get their mask from numpy's isnan, the library builds with -fno-finite-math-only, and tests/test_prior.py checks training prior == live prior bit for bit with exact zeros off the mask. Re-check on 64 rows: 0 of 1,756 ungraded entries with prior > 0. Exactness gate still 1000/1000. The student is refit from scratch on all labels; all earlier student results (rounds 1-23) were trained on the wrong prior.
decisions.rejected: Keep the old student and only fix new labels

decisions.title: Action teacher beats c2 too; student paused; combined teacher next
decisions.text: Action teacher only (c2 buys; every action decision incl. stop graded by 32 paired rollouts to the end, gain > 2 SE and > 0.02): 56.2% vs c2 over 200 games (95% interval 51.5-60.8%), overriding 2.2% of action decisions (160 other action, 69 stop instead of play, 0 play instead of stop). The student (p1, flat for 6 rounds at ~50% dev) is paused so 7 workers can measure the combined teacher (buys + actions) vs c2. Resume p1 with --continue.
decisions.rejected: Keep the student collecting: no progress since round 18

decisions.title: Training OOM-killed at round 22; student loss now led by the paired gain
decisions.text: The fit held all 344k positions twice and scored the whole dev split in one pass (4.6 GB peak, kernel OOM kill at 12:48; no labels lost). Now: preallocated load shared with torch, dev in chunks. The student had plateaued since round 18 (dev ~50%, regret 0.051 vs c2's 0.045), so the absolute win-chance fit is down-weighted to 0.1 and the paired-gain term (prediction of Q_a - Q_c2, weighted by 1/SE^2) leads.
decisions.rejected: More rounds unchanged: no movement over the last 4 rounds

decisions.title: Speed-up: sparse transposed net for rollouts (C), 2.2x end to end
decisions.text: gprof: the network was 83% of teacher time, the engine under 3%. Bake-off on 400 recorded positions: C sparse 2.85x per forward, Rust 1.6x, both 400/400 same argmax. End to end 62 -> 137 rollouts/s per process; labels 4.2-6.2 -> 10.7 positions/s on 5 workers. Exactness gate: 1,000/1,000 identical games. Label workers now spawned (356 MB in all instead of ~940 MB each).
decisions.rejected: Rust port (slower here: no float reassociation); float16 weights (would change the policy); a GPU (batch 1, serial)

decisions.title: Student chooses among the teacher's candidates, with c2's preference as input
decisions.text: Round 1 student overrode 76% of buys and scored 0.2% at margin 0: it was trained only on the graded candidates (c2's top 5 + PASS) but picked among all legal cards, including ones it never saw labelled. Now it ranks the same candidate set, and each card token carries c2's probability of buying it, so the student starts near c2 and learns corrections
decisions.rejected: Wait for more data: would not fix choices outside the labelled set

decisions.title: Teacher gate 1 lost; keep going with a z-gate and the student
decisions.text: Gate 1 (16-32 draws, margin 0.04): 41.5% after 100 games vs c2, overriding 22% of buys on noise (winner's curse). Gate 2 requires a gain of 2 paired SEs at 32 draws. The student run p1 starts at once: averaging unbiased labels across positions removes the per-position noise; its dev match every round is the test
decisions.rejected: Stop the experiment: the proposal's rule, but the failure is explained by noise in single-position play, which distillation addresses

decisions.title: Gate the teacher before distilling
decisions.text: Play the rollout teacher itself against c2 first: if exact-ish rollout values cannot beat c2, a student of them cannot either
decisions.rejected: Start with the student pilot and the controls (imitation, flat MLP) as in the proposal: postponed to save compute
